reviewer.agent: Claude Code (file handoff; environment names the handoff channel)

themes.label: Militarization through autonomous weapons
themes.definition: AI risks framed in terms of militarization, including autonomous weapons.
themes.inclusion: Include passages naming autonomous weapons or militarization as an AI risk.
themes.exclusion: Exclude general safety concerns about opaque models not linked to military use.
themes.boundary_cases: Lists that include militarization among several AI risks count here as well as in other risk codes.

themes.label: Opaque models need safeguards before critical tasks
themes.definition: Concern that poorly understood AI models should not be entrusted with critical tasks without robust safeguards, with catastrophic framing.
themes.inclusion: Include passages about AI interpretability, safeguards for critical uses, or catastrophic outcomes from unsafe AI.
themes.exclusion: Exclude military-only framing, which goes to AI_MILITARY_WEAPONS.
themes.boundary_cases: Hyperbolic 'destroy the world' language tied to unsafe deployment counts here.

examples.quote: As long as we do not fully understand how these models work, we cannot entrust them critical tasks without robust safeguards in place.

themes.label: Technology transfer and African AI capacity
themes.definition: Calls for technology and knowledge transfer, investment in connectivity, compute, research and youth training so Africa is more than a supplier of minerals.
themes.inclusion: Include passages requesting technology transfer, compute, training or partnerships to build AI capacity in developing/African states.
themes.exclusion: Exclude climate finance requests without technology content.
themes.boundary_cases: Framing about Africa not only supplying minerals for innovation hubs fits here and in AI_SOVEREIGNTY_CONCENTRATION.

examples.quote: We need to have investment in connectivity, computing capacity, scientific research, training of young people in Africa, technology transfer, governance, ethics for AI
through genuine transfer and sharing of knowledge, of technology

themes.label: Africa beyond supplying minerals
themes.definition: Concern that Africa remains a raw-material supplier to foreign innovation hubs, with calls for autonomy and African role in setting AI rules.
themes.inclusion: Include passages asserting African agency in setting AI standards or rejecting a supplier-only role.
themes.exclusion: Exclude general Security Council representation claims.
themes.boundary_cases: Calls for Africa to define international AI rules also fit AI_GLOBAL_GOVERNANCE.

examples.quote: Africa must not limit itself to supplying the minerals that fuels the world innovation hubs
our continent, Africa, can and must play an active role in defining international roles and standards

themes.label: Extraordinary opportunities, serious risks
themes.definition: AI framed as offering extraordinary opportunities alongside exclusion, manipulation and other risks.
themes.inclusion: Include passages pairing AI opportunities with explicit risks.
themes.boundary_cases: If specific risks (weapons, safety) are named, code those too.

examples.quote: Artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies offer extraordinary opportunities, but also serious risks of exclusion, manipulation of the society

value.rationale: Two Mozambique passages: 2025 gives a broad risk inventory (autonomous weapons, opaque models, manipulation) balanced against opportunity, while 2026 focuses on African capacity, technology transfer and sovereignty.
